correctness.rationale: For each vertex the source and sink probabilities are both 2^{-degree}; the only nonzero off-diagonal source–sink covariance terms occur on adjacent pairs and equal q_u q_v. Summation yields the identity. Star minimum follows from degree/leaf inequalities and two guaranteed leaf edges. A terminal branch-vertex pendant-path transplant strictly increases covariance by at least 5/64 (or 13/64 if leaf-neighbor), reduces integer branching excess, and terminates at the path. The n=2,3 exceptions and all bounds are handled exactly. Exact orientation enumeration through n=9 and exhaustive tree extremal checks through n=12 agree; these computations are not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The natural dependence statistic on uniformly oriented fixed trees can be negative, zero, or positive depending on graph shape. The theorem gives sharp all-order extremizers and a five-vertex onset with an explicit shape-changing mechanism. It goes beyond routine indicator covariance calculation, which alone cannot compare graphs, and the structural strict-transplant lemma has mathematical content and plausible relevance to source–sink dependence and oriented-tree statistics.
